## Tidepool landing page build plan

1. **Navigation** — A slim, full-width header with Tidepool’s wordmark on the left and “How it works,” “For teams,” and “Sign in” on the right. Set “Start planning” as a solid button. Use a warm off-white background, ink-blue text, and a clean sans serif.

2. **Hero** — Two-column layout: copy on the left, a large, crisp product mockup on the right. Show a shared weekly plan with a few color-coded tasks and teammates’ initials—not a day-by-day sidebar. Headline: **“Make a week your whole team can see.”** Supporting copy: “Bring priorities, owners, and plans into one calm place—so everyone knows what’s next.” CTA: **“Plan your week”**, with a quieter “See how it works” link. Use deep ocean blue, pale aqua, and a small citrus accent; keep the illustration geometric and understated.

3. **Value proposition** — Centered section with three evenly spaced cards: **“Agree on priorities,” “Know who owns what,”** and **“Adjust without losing the plot.”** Pair each with a simple, original line icon. Keep copy short and focused on everyday team benefits; avoid promising automatic integrations or features not established.

4. **Product walkthrough** — Alternate text and interface crops across two rows. Show a team setting weekly priorities, assigning work, then reshuffling plans. Use subtle connector lines and highlighted UI details to guide the eye. Copy should describe a simple flow: “Set the focus. Share the work. Revisit it together.”

5. **Team perspective** — A full-width pale-blue band with a short, attributed customer quote if approved. Use a large editorial serif for the quote and a small sans-serif attribution—never fabricate a testimonial. If no quote is available, use a concise product principle instead.

6. **Final CTA** — Centered close with the headline **“Start the week on the same page.”** Repeat the primary CTA and include a low-pressure reassurance about getting started.

7. **Footer** — Wordmark, compact navigation, and legal links. Maintain generous spacing and strong contrast throughout; use responsive stacked layouts on small screens.

## Tidepool landing page build plan

1. **Header** — Keep the navigation quiet and useful: Tidepool wordmark left; “How it works” and “For teams” links, “Sign in,” and a high-contrast **“Start planning”** button right. Use a warm ivory canvas, deep navy text, and generous spacing.

2. **Hero** — Use a two-column layout: direct, benefit-led copy on the left; a large, believable weekly-planning interface on the right. Show a Monday–Friday board with a few team priorities, owners, and a visible week-at-a-glance—not a calendar sidebar or decorative dashboard collage. Headline: **“Get your team on the same page for the week.”** Follow with: “Set priorities together, make ownership clear, and adjust plans as the week changes.” Primary CTA: **“Plan your week”**; secondary link: **“See how it works.”** Add a small caption under the mockup: “One shared view of the week.” Use ocean blue, soft aqua, and a restrained warm-coral accent. Set headlines in a distinctive humanist sans; keep interface labels and body copy highly legible.

3. **The problem, made tangible** — A short, centered transition: **“The week gets easier when the plan is shared.”** Beneath it, show three compact before-and-after moments—unclear priorities / agreed focus, scattered ownership / visible owners, plans that drift / a shared way to revisit them. Use simple diagrams rather than stock photography.

4. **How it works** — Three numbered steps in a horizontal row on desktop, stacked on mobile: **Choose the focus. Share the work. Revisit the week.** Pair each with a close crop of the relevant interface state. Keep explanations practical and brief; don’t imply integrations or automation unless verified.

5. **Team benefit** — Use a full-width pale-aqua band with one approved customer quote and attribution. If no quote is available, replace it with a product principle: **“A useful weekly plan is one the whole team can actually use.”** Set this moment apart with an editorial serif accent and ample whitespace; don’t invent social proof.

6. **Closing CTA** — Return to the ivory canvas. Headline: **“Make next week clearer.”** Repeat **“Plan your week”** and add a factual, low-friction reassurance beneath it.

7. **Footer** — Wordmark, anchor links, sign-in, and legal links. Maintain strong contrast, responsive layouts, and a clear primary action throughout.
